problem: A particle moves in a uniform gravitational field from the origin with an acceleration of $-10j\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}$ and an initial velocity of $(-i+5j)\,\text{m/s}.$ Find the position vector of the particle after $3$ seconds.

feedback.problem: A particle moves from the origin with an acceleration of $6i\,{\text{km/h}}^{2}$ and an initial velocity of $-5j\,\text{km/h}.$ Find the position vector of the particle after $3$ hours.
feedback.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant acceleration $a,$ the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
r={r}_{0}+ut+\frac{1}{2}a{t}^{2},
$$

 

where ${r}_{0}$ is the initial position of the particle and $u$ is its initial velocity.

In our case, we have

$$
{r}_{0}=0i+0j,\,u=-5j,\,a=6i.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the particle after $t=3\,\text{h}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =(0i+0j)+(-5j)(3)+\frac{1}{2}(6i)(3)^{2} \\  & =-15j+27i \\  & =(27i-15j)\,\text{km}.\end{aligned}
$$
